decision_flags.title: Suspected unstable angina managed as outpatient?
decision_flags.concern: The working diagnosis is unstable angina, yet the plan is a cardiology visit next week with a stress test; unstable angina usually calls for same-day evaluation, and stress testing is generally avoided until it is ruled out. If the pattern is truly stable exertional angina, the label and urgency differ.
decision_flags.consider: You might clarify whether the pain is stable or crescendo/at rest and, if unstable angina remains the suspicion, consider same-day ED or urgent cardiology evaluation with troponin.

decision_flags.title: Hydrochlorothiazide without BP reading or baseline labs
decision_flags.concern: HCTZ was started while hypertension is not yet confirmed, with no blood pressure value or kidney function and electrolytes mentioned; in a diabetic patient a thiazide can raise glucose and lower potassium, and the edema has not been worked up.
decision_flags.consider: You might document today's BP, check a BMP and urine albumin, and consider whether an ACE inhibitor or ARB would suit her diabetes better.
